anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves all three facts from fails to holds, which is exactly the Change's intent: Before explicitly rejected `deliver-nits` as an unrecognized grant, ignored the record's caps, and rendered a final menu at 1111... without dispatching anything, so N1/N2 were never fixed and N3 never surfaced. After treats the retained course as standing authority, dispatches fresh helpers for N1 and N2 in iteration 1 (f1), lets the Minor finding at src/guard.mjs:20 become N3 that fails the exit check and starts iteration 2 without a new pick (f2), and only renders final once N1/N2/N3 all have resolved closure lines, the refresh resolves CI-sufficient on the exact head 3333..., and merge is left as a separate numeric pick (f3). Nothing regressed relative to Before since Before held none of these facts. Two small wording points to keep this robust: the final report should state explicitly that the course remains `deliver-nits` (After only implies it by never changing it), and the round accounting narration should tie `rounds_used` increments to the new source commits per wave (it does, but say 'one round per wave with new source commits' rather than letting a reader infer two helpers might cost two rounds).

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: All three facts move from fails to holds, exactly as the Change intended. Before treated the retained deliver-nits course as expired one-shot authority, dispatched nothing for N1/N2, and rendered a final menu with the nits still open, so none of the facts held. After reads the retained course as persistent authority: it dispatches fresh implementers for N1 and N2 despite the already-mergeable head, pushes to 2222..., runs the fresh comment-source review that mints N3, states that the retained deliver-nits course includes N3 automatically with no new selection, repairs it, pushes to 3333..., and only then renders final after every closure line is resolved, exact-head CI is green and the worktree matches the remote, while merge stays a separate numeric pick. One small tightening for the After wording: state explicitly at the final menu that the persisted course is still `deliver-nits` (rather than leaving it implied by 'retained course'), and keep the explicit line that the final menu offers merge without executing it; both are already present in substance, so no fact is at risk, but naming the surviving course at exit makes f3 unambiguous for a reader checking the record state.
